transcript.text: Bosch induction hob PUE611BB1E making a loud buzzing/humming noise when I put my big stockpot on high. Is it about to break?

It is very unlikely to be about to break. Induction hobs naturally produce a buzzing or humming sound at high power because the magnetic field interacts with the metal in the base of your cookware; this is especially common with large, heavy stockpots and is considered normal behaviour. The main thing we need to rule out is whether the pot itself is vibrating against the glass (which can amplify noise) or if there is a genuine electrical fault. Please check two things: first, ensure the bottom of your stockpot is completely flat and dry so it sits firmly without wobbling; second, try running that zone at high power with a smaller, lighter pan to see if the noise level changes significantly.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.

Thanks. I tried a lighter pan: my cheap frying pan is also noisy on high, but my heavy cast iron pot is quiet. The stockpot base looks flat, a sandwich base, maybe slightly smaller than the ring. No burning smell or error codes, and it's much quieter at 6 and below.

This suggests it is probably normal behaviour. Induction hobs work by creating a magnetic field that makes the metal in your pan vibrate at high frequency; this creates the buzzing sound you hear. The fact that the cheap frying pan (likely thinner steel) buzzes more than the heavy cast iron pot (which has higher mass and dampens vibration) is classic induction behaviour, not a fault. Burning smells, or cracking sounds, your hob is fine. You can place a silicone mat under the pans to reduce any rattling against the glass if it bothers you.
